notes.title: PRID spellings that differ only by case are not linked
notes.body: In 13 spellings the PRID of SOTERsummaryFile rows (82 rows) differs from the PRID of SOTERparameterEstimates only by upper or lower case. Raw view: spellings as in the source and no link between them (decision B3 of #69, 2026-10-13): these summary rows have no estimate layer in soil_core.v_sotwis_estimate_links, and 6 estimate profiles (25 layers) are reached by no summary row of the same spelling. The pairs are listed in details. The revised view (#68, rule R6) links them without regard to case.
notes.decision: https://github.com/giulange/global-soil-data-hub/issues/69

notes.title: Negative values are gap codes of the source, published unchanged
notes.body: Negative values of the soil parameters are the gap codes of the source and are published unchanged (decision B5 of #69): -1 in Brazil, SOVEUR v2, Jordan, Kenya, Latin America and the Caribbean, Southern Africa and the Indo-Gangetic Plains; -9 in Senegal and The Gambia, Tunisia and Upper Tana; -3 and -7 in Central Africa (-7 in its non-soil rows). ISRIC Report 2004/04 (p.25, note 4) documents -1, Reports 2008/05 (p.30, note 4), 2010/01 (p.30) and 2010/07b (p.24) document -9, as gaps the taxotransfer scheme could not fill; Reports 2007/02 (p.25, note 4) and 2005/04 (p.23, note 4) mention negative values without a code; the other reports say nothing. CECc is set to -9 where clay is 5 % or less (Reports 2008/05 p.25, 2010/01 p.25, 2010/07b p.20). Counts per table and dataset in details.
notes.decision: https://github.com/giulange/global-soil-data-hub/issues/69

notes.title: SOTERsummaryFile_Prop and SOTERsummaryFile_Prop_T1S1 (raw layer only)
notes.body: SOTERsummaryFile_Prop (one row per soil component) and SOTERsummaryFile_Prop_T1S1 (one row per unit, TCID 1 / SCID 1; the reports call it SOTERsummaryFile_PROP_SC1) of Senegal and The Gambia, Tunisia and Upper Tana hold the values of SOTERsummaryFile with the layers D1-D5 across columns (ISRIC Report 2008/05, App. 5 p.31): every value equals the summary row (D4_ELCO stored as text, numerically equal). They stay in the raw layer (decision B9 of #69).

datasets.name: sotwis_estimates
datasets.title: SOTWIS estimate profiles
datasets.description: SOTWIS soil parameter estimates per representative profile (SOTERparameterEstimates of the 11 SOTWIS packages): one feature/profile per (dataset, PRID), one layer per source row (D1-D5), the values of the source row; no geometry (the profiles are reached by CLAF and PRID from the soil components of the map units). The summary rows of sotwis_components keep their own values (decision B2 of #69); the taxotransfer flags of each layer are served by GET /sotwis/ttr-flags.

notes.title: PRID spellings that differ only by case are not linked
notes.body: In 13 spellings the PRID of SOTERsummaryFile rows (82 rows) differs from the PRID of SOTERparameterEstimates only by upper or lower case. Raw view: spellings as in the source and no link between them (decision B3 of #69, 2026-10-13): these summary rows have no estimate layer in soil_core.v_sotwis_estimate_links, and 6 estimate profiles (25 layers) are reached by no summary row of the same spelling. The pairs are listed in details. The revised view (#68, rule R6) links them without regard to case.
notes.decision: https://github.com/giulange/global-soil-data-hub/issues/69

notes.title: Negative values are gap codes of the source, published unchanged
notes.body: Negative values of the soil parameters are the gap codes of the source and are published unchanged (decision B5 of #69): -1 in Brazil, SOVEUR v2, Jordan, Kenya, Latin America and the Caribbean, Southern Africa and the Indo-Gangetic Plains; -9 in Senegal and The Gambia, Tunisia and Upper Tana; -3 and -7 in Central Africa (-7 in its non-soil rows). ISRIC Report 2004/04 (p.25, note 4) documents -1, Reports 2008/05 (p.30, note 4), 2010/01 (p.30) and 2010/07b (p.24) document -9, as gaps the taxotransfer scheme could not fill; Reports 2007/02 (p.25, note 4) and 2005/04 (p.23, note 4) mention negative values without a code; the other reports say nothing. CECc is set to -9 where clay is 5 % or less (Reports 2008/05 p.25, 2010/01 p.25, 2010/07b p.20). Counts per table and dataset in details.
notes.decision: https://github.com/giulange/global-soil-data-hub/issues/69

notes.title: Taxotransfer flags (SOTERflagTTRrules)
notes.body: The taxotransfer and expert-rule flags of SOTERflagTTRrules (35881 rows) are served by GET /sotwis/ttr-flags, one row per estimate profile, layer and sub-layer, codes verbatim, with the legend at GET /sotwis/ttr-flags/legend (decision B6 of #69). The expert-rule column is TTRfinal in 31848 rows (Brazil, SOVEUR v2, Jordan, Kenya, Latin America and the Caribbean, Southern Africa, Indo-Gangetic Plains) and TTRexpert in 4033 rows (Central Africa, Senegal and The Gambia, Tunisia, Upper Tana): both names are kept (decision B7; Report 2007/02, p.22, calls the Central Africa column TTRfinal). A flag does not attach one-to-one to a value: a layer may hold several sub-layer rows (Newtopdep, Newbotdep) with different flags, while the estimate is one value per layer. Central Africa RWns1 has five estimate rows with Layer '-' (every value -7) and flag rows for D1-D5: those flag rows have no estimate layer.
notes.decision: https://github.com/giulange/global-soil-data-hub/issues/69

notes.title: Estimates and summary rows keep their own values
notes.body: Every table keeps its own values (decision B2 of #69): the summary rows of sotwis_components are not replaced by the estimates. Compared on the same dataset, CLAF, PRID and Layer, 4390 summary rows differ in CECc and 2938 in ELCO, all in Senegal and The Gambia, Tunisia and Upper Tana, whose summary rows hold these two values as integers (no report mentions the rounding); SOTERsummaryFile_T1S1D1 keeps the decimals of ELCO. 64 estimate layers (15 profiles) reach no summary row of the same spelling: profiles named in no unit composition (Brazil BRamRM13/P18; Kenya KE117/1-9, KE117/2-1, KE162/3-141, KE162/3-356, KE177/2-12, KE192/2-8, KESYN79, KESYN97) and the case variants of note prid_case_spellings.

notes.title: Empty estimate columns
notes.body: The SOTERparameterEstimates columns TAWK (9 datasets) and MCT0, MCT1, MCT5 (Tunisia) and the CNrt column of Tunisia hold no value (every cell null): nothing to expose. TAWK is undocumented in every report read.

notes.title: Unit attributes: landform, lithology, slope (terrain)
notes.body: The components of a polygon carry the attributes of its map unit as source_attributes (component_attributes on the observation rows), namespaced unit.<source column>, values verbatim (decision B11 of #69): LNDF (landform), LITH (lithology) and SLOP (slope, %) of the terrain tables Terrain-shrt (Brazil, SOVEUR v2, Latin America and the Caribbean), Terrain (Jordan), TERRAIN-shrt (Indo-Gangetic Plains) and terrain (Kenya: columns LNDF_, LITH_, SLOP_ and WATER_TOWN, one row per polygon, matched to the polygon by its position); LNDF and LITH of SOTERunitComposition for Central Africa, Senegal and The Gambia, Tunisia and Upper Tana. SOVEUR v2 gives LNDF and LITH for 1,443 of 8,361 units and no SLOP; Southern Africa has no terrain information. The meaning of WATER_TOWN (L, R, T, W) is undocumented. The definitions are those of the SOTER Procedures Manual (landform, lithology, slope); the codes are listed in the SOTWIS_codes code list (GET /code-lists/SOTWIS_codes) and the SOTER Codes table. Not exposed, for lack of a soil component to carry them: the terrain rows of the 27 Kenya water and town polygons (KE7000-KE7012, KE8000-KE8023) and the attributes of 24 units that have no polygon in the database (per dataset in details).
notes.decision: https://github.com/giulange/global-soil-data-hub/issues/69

notes.title: Brazilian Legal Amazon subset
notes.body: The 193 units listed by SOTERunits (Brazilian Legal Amazon) carry unit.subset = 'Brazilian Legal Amazon' on the components of their 561 polygons (decision B8 of #69). ISRIC Report 2004/03 (p.ii, p.10) gives 193 units and 571 polygons for the subset clipped from the Brazil set; the database has 561 polygons for these units: the difference is not explained by the report. The other three tables of the subset (SOTERsummaryFile, SOTERsummaryFile_T1S1D1 and SOTERunitComposition (Brazilian Legal Amazon)) repeat rows of the Brazil tables and stay in the raw layer.
notes.decision: https://github.com/giulange/global-soil-data-hub/issues/69

notes.title: SOTWIS_codes code list
notes.body: The SOTWIS_codes table (ATTRIBUTE, CODE, DESCRIPTION) is kept as its own code list, as in the source (decision B10 of #69): GET /code-lists/SOTWIS_codes, 1527 rows from 3 packages (Senegal and The Gambia, Tunisia, Upper Tana), the same 509 triples in each. It explains the codes of CLAF, CLAF_m (major soil groups), DRAI, ISOC, LITH, LNDF and PHAS; ISRIC Reports 2008/05 (p.23) and 2010/07b (p.18) only name it.
notes.decision: https://github.com/giulange/global-soil-data-hub/issues/69

notes.title: SOTERunitCompCOMPACT (raw layer only)
notes.body: SOTERunitCompCOMPACT (Central Africa, 244 rows: NEWSUID, SoilMapUnit) repeats the SoilMapUnit code of SOTERunitComposition without its ' [NEWSUID]' suffix (244 of 244); it stays in the raw layer (decision B12 of #69). The composition code is served as soil_map_unit.
notes.decision: https://github.com/giulange/global-soil-data-hub/issues/69

notes.title: Other SOTERunitComposition columns (raw layer only)
notes.body: The SOTERunitComposition columns WATE, DomFAOgroup, NoSoilComp, PropDomFAOgroup and PropSynthProf (Central Africa, Senegal and The Gambia, Tunisia, Upper Tana) are not exposed; they stay in the raw layer.
